paragraphs:
(Hyman places him among the amoraim in the Land of Israel, in the fourth generation.)
R' Eliezer and R' Avdimi are mentioned, both in the name of R' Mana, in Eruvin ch. 10 halakhah 2. Hyman identifies this R' Mana as of the second generation, and R' Elazar is the son of R' Yose, the colleague of R' Yonah. This is also demonstrated from Shabbat ch. 5 halakhah 4, where R' Avdimi spoke together with R' Hanina. The earlier R' Hanina and R-Ch bar Ada, Bar Kappara’s sister’s son, belonged to the first generation of amoraim; Hyman nevertheless identifies, without doubt, the Chanina here as the later Chanina, R' Mana’s colleague, and the R-Ch bar Ada here as the later R-Ch bar Ada, who disputes with R' Mani in Bava Batra, beginning of ch. 10, and see there: R' Ami the Babylonian said, "Let us hear it from this," and afterwards R' Avdimi said, "Let us hear it from this." Hyman states that it is known that R' Ami the Babylonian was afterwards in Babylonia in the days of R' Ashi. We also find in Terumot ch. 1 halakhah 1 "R' Avdimi said," and that same statement is repeated in Gittin ch. 7 halakhah 1 in the name of R' Abba Mari. Likewise in Yevamot ch. 13 halakhah 1 "R' Avdimi said," and it is repeated there ch. 1 halakhah 4 in the name of R-A Mari, since R' Abba Mari was also a colleague of R' Elazar b. R' Yose, as explained in his entry. And in Bava Batra ch. 9 halakhah 1 "R' Avdimi said," and it is repeated in Ketubot ch. 13 halakhah 3 in the name of R' Abba; and Hyman suggests that the word "Mari" is missing and says it should read R' Abba Mari.
